heroText: Vientiane works best as a base in Laos when you anchor days around Pha That Luang, Patuxai and Wat Si Saket. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Vientiane Wattay handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

stayOverview: Start with Mekong Riverside for the easiest first Vientiane stay, then compare Chanthabouly and Sisattanak when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Vientiane hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use Mekong Riverside for sightseeing, Chanthabouly for a different local base, and Sisattanak or That Luang when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Vientiane unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Mekong Riverside for a first stay because it keeps main sights, restaurants and practical local movement close.

travelTips.title: Airport timing
travelTips.text: Leave extra time for Vientiane Wattay, especially for early flights, late arrivals, traffic or unfamiliar transfer routes.

travelTips.title: Local movement
travelTips.text: Plan each day in clusters around Pha That Luang and Patuxai so transfers do not consume the best sightseeing hours.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Keep one flexible slot for nearby routes from Vientiane, checking weather, transport and opening hours before committing.

history.label: 6th century
history.text: Other romanisations include "Viangchan" and "Wiangchan". Dvaravati city state kingdoms By the 6th century in the Chao Phraya River Valley, Mon peoples had coalesced to create the Dvaravati kingdoms.

history.label: Modern city
history.text: In Lao, viang (ວຽງ) refers to a 'walled city' whereas chan (ຈັນ, previously ຈັນທນ໌) derives from Sanskrit candana (चन्दन, /t͡ɕand̪ana/), 'sandalwood' and can be translated as the 'walled city of sandalwood'.

history.label: Today
history.text: Some believe it refers to the 'walled city of the moon' as chan can represent 'moon', and this was previously distinguished in writing as "ຈັນທຣ໌".

history.label: Regional role
history.text: In the north, Haripunjaya (Lamphun) emerged as a rival power to the Dvaravati.
